idea: Week three, from the story bank: written from the source, then corrected by two independent editors before voicing.
description: Karnataka's output per person at 2011-12 prices rose from ₹90,263 in 2011-12 to ₹1,91,970 in 2023-24: 2.1 times. Maharashtra's rose 1.7 times, from ₹99,597 to ₹1,66,013. Karnataka went from 9% below Maharashtra to 16% above, and was at least 15% above in each of the last three years.

The measure is net state domestic product per person: a state average of output, not what households earn. Andhra Pradesh, Telangana and Jammu and Kashmir are blank on the map because their boundaries changed; Gujarat has no 2023-24 figure.
source: National Statistics Office, Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation, as published in the RBI Handbook of Statistics on Indian States, Table 20: per capita net state domestic product at constant prices (base 2011-12), rupees a year. A state average, not household income. Gujarat has no figure for 2023-24; Andhra Pradesh and Telangana are left off the map because the state was split in 2014, and Jammu and Kashmir because its boundary changed in 2019.
